walkthrough: This PR introduces a complete S3-backed ChatMemoryRepository implementation for Spring AI, enabling persistent storage of conversation messages as JSON documents in Amazon S3 and S3-compatible services. The implementation includes configuration properties, the core repository with CRUD operations, Spring Boot auto-configuration, comprehensive integration tests using LocalStack, and full documentation covering setup, configuration, and best practices.

changes.summary: S3ChatMemoryProperties defines auto-configuration properties (bucket name, region, key prefix, storage class, initialization flag) under spring.ai.chat.memory.repository.s3 prefix. S3ChatMemoryConfig encapsulates S3Client, bucket configuration, optional key resolver and conversation ID extractor functions with builder-based instantiation and cross-field validation.

ChatMemoryRepository implementation using AWS S3 for persistence. Handles lazy bucket verification via double-checked locking, serializes/deserializes messages to/from JSON with type-specific message reconstruction, lists conversation IDs via S3 pagination, loads/saves/deletes conversations via GetObject/PutObject/DeleteObject, and supports custom key resolution patterns with optional keyResolver and conversationIdExtractor functions.

Conditional S3Client and S3ChatMemoryRepository bean registration, enabled when S3Client classpath, bucket-name property, and configuration properties are available. Supports region configuration and optional S3 endpoint override via system property. Both beans skip creation if user provides custom beans.

ApplicationContextRunner-based tests verify bean creation/absence with/without bucket-name property, property binding into S3ChatMemoryProperties, custom S3Client bean usage, storage-class default/override behavior using LocalStack S3 test fixture.

LocalStack S3-based end-to-end tests covering full CRUD flow, conversation ID listing/pagination, message metadata and ordering preservation, storage class configuration, content encoding robustness (special characters, Unicode, large payloads), bucket initialization lifecycle, custom key/namespace patterns (product/date, actor/session), builder validation for resolver/extractor pairing.

README documents features, Maven/Gradle setup, configuration examples (auto-config and manual builder), custom S3 endpoint setup, configuration properties table, S3 operational considerations (consistency, cost, security), error handling, testing strategies, and troubleshooting. Antora documentation covers S3ChatMemoryRepository usage, credentials, and dynamic key resolution with examples. Parent POM registers new modules; BOM adds managed dependencies; starter POM wires Spring Boot and Spring AI S3 chat memory artifacts.

issues.content: Pin the LocalStack image tag to avoid flaky integration tests. S3ChatMemoryAutoConfigurationIT uses localstack/localstack:latest, while other integration tests in this repo already pin localstack/localstack:3.5.0; update this test to use the pinned version for deterministic CI.

Remove the unused messages variable (PMD) or actually exercise the repository. messages is constructed but never used, so the comment about "should not throw" isn't validated—only a non-null assertion runs. Either drop the dead variable (and the now-unused Message/UserMessage imports) or invoke a repository operation to genuinely test the custom S3Client path.

Apply markdown formatting fixes for consistency. The markdown linter has identified several minor formatting issues: missing blank lines around fenced code blocks (lines 79, 85, 249, 276, 298) and a missing trailing newline at the end of the file (line 439). While these don't affect functionality, fixing them improves consistency and ensures proper rendering across all markdown parsers. As per coding guidelines, markdown files should follow standard formatting conventions flagged by markdownlint-cli2. Also applies to: 85-85, 249-249, 276-276, 298-298, 439-439

Document that REDUCED_REDUNDANCY storage class is deprecated. AWS deprecated the REDUCED_REDUNDANCY storage class and recommends using STANDARD instead, as it's more cost-effective. This should be noted to prevent users from selecting a suboptimal option.

TOOL messages silently lose their content on round-trip. serialize stores message.getText() for every message, but createMessage reconstructs TOOL messages with responses(List.of()), discarding the persisted content. A conversation containing tool responses will not survive a save→load cycle intact. The javadoc documents this, but it is still silent data loss for a persistence layer. Consider serializing the structured ToolResponse objects (id/name/responseData) so they can be faithfully reconstructed, instead of flattening to content.

Pin the LocalStack image to a fixed version (don’t use :latest) In S3ChatMemoryRepositoryIT.initializeLocalStack (.../S3ChatMemoryRepositoryIT.java lines 56-60), localstack/localstack:latest tracks the latest stable release and will change over time, so the integration test isn’t fully reproducible. Pin to a specific tag (e.g., 2026.05.0).

Prefer a collision-proof unique prefix. System.currentTimeMillis() has millisecond resolution and is reused for inline prefixes in several tests (Lines 265, 344, 382, 425, 472, 527). Since multiple tests assert exact listing sizes (hasSize(5), hasSize(25), containsExactly(...)) and the bucket is shared across tests, any prefix overlap would cross-contaminate findConversationIds() results and cause flakiness. UUID.randomUUID() removes the risk entirely.

walkthrough: This PR adds a complete new Bedrock Knowledge Base vector store to Spring AI. The implementation includes a read-only VectorStore backed by AWS Bedrock Agent Runtime, Spring Boot auto-configuration with configurable properties, metadata filtering via filter expression conversion, comprehensive testing, and user documentation.

changes.summary: Add BEDROCK_KNOWLEDGE_BASE type constant and register the auto-configuration class for Spring's discovery.

Implement BedrockKnowledgeBaseVectorStore with similarity search, pagination, result conversion to Spring Document, metadata extraction from Bedrock location types, and BedrockKnowledgeBaseFilterExpressionConverter for mapping Spring AI filter expressions to Bedrock RetrievalFilter objects.

Comprehensive unit tests covering filter expression conversion (null, comparison, list, logical operators), builder validation, search result mapping, score threshold filtering, pagination, AWS exception propagation, and location type metadata extraction.

Define BedrockKnowledgeBaseVectorStoreProperties with configurable knowledgeBaseId, region, topK, similarityThreshold, searchType, and rerankingModelArn; create auto-configuration bean factories for BedrockAgentRuntimeClient and BedrockKnowledgeBaseVectorStore.
Create new Maven modules for vector store implementation, auto-configuration, and Spring Boot starter; update root pom module list and BOM dependency management entries.

Add comprehensive documentation covering prerequisites, Spring Boot auto-configuration, configuration properties, SEMANTIC/HYBRID search types, reranking, metadata filtering with examples, manual configuration, native client access, limitations (read-only, region constraints), and supported data sources.

Integration tests with live Bedrock Knowledge Base, validating search behavior, result structure, topK enforcement, similarity threshold filtering, unsupported write operations, SEMANTIC/HYBRID search types, and filter expressions.

issues.content: Test gating on AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID is too narrow and contradicts the Javadoc. The beans use DefaultCredentialsProvider.create(), which resolves credentials from many sources (static keys, SSO, instance profile, web identity, container roles). Gating on AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID means anyone authenticating via SSO/instance-profile/etc. will have these tests silently skipped despite having valid credentials. The Javadoc (Lines 44-49) also lists AWS_REGION as a requirement and never mentions AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, so the code and docs are inconsistent. Consider gating only on BEDROCK_KB_ID (the truly required input) and letting the credential chain fail loudly if no credentials are present, or align the Javadoc with the actual gating condition.

walkthrough: This PR applies two independent performance optimizations to Spring AI model utilities. ModelOptionsUtils refactors reflection-based method name handling to use Set collection instead of List, and DefaultToolCallingManager replaces streaming checks with set-based deduplication for tool name lookups.

changes.summary: Method and Set imports support collecting sourceInterfaceClazz method names into a Set via Method::getName in mergeBeans. The toGetName helper is simplified to use Character.toUpperCase(name.charAt(0)).

Set and Collectors imports support precomputing existingToolNames as a deduplicated set of tool names from ToolCallbacks. The resolveToolDefinitions method replaces per-tool streaming anyMatch checks with efficient set membership tests.

walkthrough: This PR refines the MCP Server Boot Starters documentation by adjusting formatting in the introduction and annotations sections, and adds a new guide section on configuring McpTransportContext to pass transport-specific metadata to tool methods, including a working example.

changes.summary: Line breaks adjusted in the introductory paragraph about Spring AI auto-configuration, @McpResource bullet entry normalized, and trailing whitespace removed from the auto-configuration steps.

Added "Adding data to McpTransportContext" section explaining default McpTransportContext.EMPTY, configuring a TransportContextExtractor via WebMvcStreamableServerTransportProvider, and example code for reading transport headers inside tool methods.

issues.content: Preserve auto-configured transport settings when overriding WebMvcStreamableServerTransportProvider The docs example replaces the transport provider with only contextExtractor(...) and omits the same builder fields that auto-config normally sets (jsonMapper, mcpEndpoint, keepAliveInterval, disallowDelete). Because a custom @Bean bypasses McpServerStreamableHttpWebMvcAutoConfiguration, any user configuration for spring.ai.mcp.server.streamable-http.* for those options won’t be applied.

Guard the Authorization header before using it in Map.of. serverRequest.headers().firstHeader("Authorization") is @Nullable and returns null when the header is missing, and Map.of(...) throws a NullPointerException if any value is null. Update the example to handle the missing-header case (e.g., return McpTransportContext.EMPTY).

walkthrough: This PR enhances MCP tool result handling to parse JSON arrays of content objects into typed MCP Content subtypes (text, image, audio, resource links) rather than always wrapping results as plain text. It adds a new parseContentList method to McpToolUtils, integrates it into tool result handling, and provides comprehensive test coverage for both the parsing logic and the tool specification integration.

changes.summary: parseContentList method adds ArrayList and JsonNode imports, logger infrastructure, and implements conversion of JSON arrays into typed Content objects (TextContent, ImageContent, AudioContent, ResourceLink), with fallback to TextContent for non-array inputs and parse errors. ParseContentListTests provides comprehensive test coverage for all content type parsing paths, mixed content arrays, embedded resources, and edge cases.

changes.layer: Integrate parseContentList into tool result handling
changes.summary: Tool result handling in toSyncToolSpecification now calls parseContentList instead of unconditionally wrapping output as single plain text. ToolUtilsTests verifies that single text, multiple text, image content, and non-JSON strings are correctly parsed and wrapped into CallToolResult with appropriate content types.

issues.content: Replace deprecated JsonNode.textValue() with asString(...) (and avoid possible mimeType NPE) in parseContentList tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode.textValue() is deprecated in Jackson 3. It can return null for non-textual/malformed nodes, and this block immediately calls mimeType.startsWith("audio"), risking an NPE. Switch these reads to asString(...): use a non-null default for mimeType (e.g., asString("")) and asString(null) for nullable fields (data, text, uri, name, title, description, mimeType). [mcp/common/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/mcp/McpToolUtils.java: parseContentList block around lines 299-324]

walkthrough: This PR adds text-to-speech support for the OpenAI SDK in Spring AI. It introduces configurable options, a TextToSpeechModel implementation that invokes the OpenAI audio API, response metadata for rate-limit handling, Spring Boot auto-configuration, and comprehensive unit and integration tests.

changes.summary: Defines TTS options with Voice and AudioResponseFormat enums, default constants, and a fluent builder. Configuration properties class provides Spring Boot integration with spring.ai.openai-sdk.audio.speech prefix and defaults for model, voice, response format, and speed.

Implements TextToSpeechModel interface with synchronous call methods that merge prompt/default options, build speech parameters, invoke the OpenAI SDK audio endpoint, read response bytes, extract rate-limit metadata from HTTP headers, and return TextToSpeechResponse. Includes option-merging helpers and fluent builder.
Adds response metadata class that parses HTTP rate-limit headers and provides OpenAiSdkRateLimit to store request/token limits, remaining counts, and reset durations.

Adds Spring Boot auto-configuration that conditionally activates when spring.ai.model.audio-speech is set to openai-sdk. Registers OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel bean, resolves connection properties, creates OpenAI client, and registers in auto-configuration manifest.
Comprehensive tests for model construction, builder variants, default option initialization, input validation (null/empty), option merging, enum constants, and mutate() immutability.
Tests for metadata header parsing covering full/partial/empty/invalid rate-limit headers, null handling, and default fallback values.
Integration tests verifying bean registration when audio-speech model is openai-sdk, no registration for other models, default property application, and custom property overrides.

End-to-end tests against OpenAI API covering basic speech generation, custom options, voice/format/speed variations, string input, stream() behavior, voice parameterization, rate-limit metadata, and model variants (tts-1, tts-1-hd).

issues.content: Back off on the TextToSpeechModel abstraction (not only OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel). In OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechAutoConfiguration (lines 44-46), the @Bean method uses a bare @ConditionalOnMissingBean, so Spring Boot checks only for an existing bean of the *return type* (OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel). Since OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel implements TextToSpeechModel, a user-supplied TextToSpeechModel won’t suppress this auto-configured bean, potentially leaving multiple TextToSpeechModel candidates. Switch to @ConditionalOnMissingBean(TextToSpeechModel.class) on that @Bean method.

Remove the real OPENAI_API_KEY gate/secret from OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechAutoConfigurationIT This class only bootstraps the Spring context and asserts bean/options; it never calls the OpenAI API. Make it run unconditionally and inject a dummy key instead of System.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") to avoid unnecessary CI skipping and secret exposure in test diagnostics.

Parse OpenAI x-ratelimit-reset-* headers as duration strings (not raw seconds). getHeaderAsDuration(...) currently does Duration.ofSeconds(Long.parseLong(...)), so if OpenAI returns values like 1s / 6m0s (per the docs) the parse throws and the method returns null, causing requestsReset/tokensReset to be lost in OpenAiSdkRateLimit. The EmptyRateLimit fallback only happens when both *-limit-* headers are absent. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits
Avoid logging the full prompt body on empty responses. prompt can contain raw user text, so this warning leaks request content into application logs.

Make stream() lazy to avoid eagerly performing the blocking HTTP call. stream() currently does Flux.just(call(prompt)), but call(TextToSpeechPrompt) performs a synchronous OpenAI request and blocks while reading the full response (openAiClient.audio().speech().create(...) and httpResponse.body().readAllBytes()). This work happens when stream() is called (not when subscribed), and any exceptions escape outside the reactive pipeline.

Merge partial defaults instead of replacing them. Passing a partial OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechOptions here drops builder defaults like voice. A caller that only overrides model or speed will later hit the Line 121 null check in call(...).
Redact the request text from toString(). input is user-supplied prompt content. Including it here makes accidental logging or exception messages leak request data.

This test never exercises the merge path. source is unused, so the test only asserts that constructor defaults were preserved. It will not catch regressions in OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel.mergeOptions(...), which is the core prompt-vs-default precedence logic.

walkthrough: This PR hardens vector store filter expression converters against injection attacks by adding dialect-specific string escaping. Each converter now escapes special characters (quotes, backslashes) before embedding string values into generated filter expressions, preventing malicious payloads from breaking out of string literals.

changes.summary: AbstractFilterExpressionConverter.doSingleValue() now uses a protected escapeStringValue() helper to escape backslashes and double quotes in deterministic order before wrapping strings in double quotes. Tests cover special character escaping, combinations, boundary cases (empty/special-only strings), and injection attack scenarios.

SimpleVectorStoreFilterExpressionConverter adds a private escapeSpELStringValue() helper that doubles single quotes for SpEL syntax safety. Tests verify SpEL injection payloads are neutralized and operator-like tokens remain literal.

AzureAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter adds an escapeODataStringValue() helper that doubles single quotes for OData syntax safety. Tests verify quote escaping prevents injection, with coverage of real-world cases like English contractions.

MariaDBFilterExpressionConverter adds a private escapeSqlStringValue() helper that escapes backslashes and doubles single quotes for SQL syntax safety. Tests verify SQL and comment-based injection payloads are neutralized, with real-world path escaping coverage.

WeaviateFilterExpressionConverter.doSingleValue() now explicitly builds valueText: and valueDate: field syntax using string concatenation and escapeStringValue(), replacing prior String.format() insertion. Tests verify quote and backslash escaping prevents payload injection.

issues.content: Escape JSON string control characters in escapeStringValue escapeStringValue only escapes \ and " while doSingleValue wraps string values in quotes, so raw U+0000–U+001F characters (e.g., newline/tab) can be emitted inside the generated JSON string literal, which is invalid per RFC 8259. testControlCharacters only checks substrings and doesn’t assert that \n/\t/\uXXXX escapes are produced, so this remains unguarded; the replacement order (\ then ") is fine.

Fix the assertion to actually detect the “}{ … {” sequence assertThat(result).doesNotMatch("\\}\\s*\\{") only checks whether the *entire* result string matches the regex (full-match semantics), so it can pass even if the sequence appears inside the expression. Use a negative containment regex assertion instead.

Consider adding an IN/NIN list-path test. These tests exercise only the single-value EQ path. The list branch (doValue List case) does not escape values, so a test covering IN/NIN with a quote-containing element would catch the residual injection gap flagged in the converter.

doesNotMatch here never fails. Same issue as in the abstract security tests: doesNotMatch requires a full-string match, so path:\[.*path:\[ can never match the complete output and this assertion always passes. It does not actually verify that a second path:[ block was prevented. Use a substring-pattern assertion.

walkthrough: This PR refactors the builder pattern across Spring AI's ChatOptions hierarchy from raw types to self-referential generics. Core contracts (ChatOptions, ToolCallingChatOptions, StructuredOutputChatOptions) now use Builder > for type-safe fluent APIs. Default implementations (DefaultChatOptions, DefaultChatOptionsBuilder, DefaultToolCallingChatOptions) are updated to store option values directly and delegate copy/mutate operations through builders. OllamaChatOptions aligns to the new pattern and adds test infrastructure validating builder and mutate semantics.

changes.layer: Core ChatOptions contract and mutate() interface
changes.summary: ChatOptions introduces a default mutate() method and generic Builder interface with @Nullable parameters and combineWith() composition; builder() returns Builder typed to DefaultChatOptionsBuilder.
DefaultChatOptions adds parameterized constructors, uses Objects.equals/hash for equality, and delegates copy()/mutate() through the builder pattern with defensive list cloning.

DefaultChatOptionsBuilder transforms from wrapping an instance to storing option fields directly; fluent setters return B via self(), stopSequences copies/clears defensively, and build() constructs fresh DefaultChatOptions. New combineWith() merges non-null builder state from compatible builders.

changes.layer: Tool calling and structured output builder contracts
changes.summary: ToolCallingChatOptions.Builder becomes generic (Builder ), extending ChatOptions.Builder with @Nullable tool callbacks/names/context setters; StructuredOutputChatOptions introduces nested Builder interface with outputSchema() method.

DefaultToolCallingChatOptions.Builder extends DefaultChatOptionsBuilder and stores tool fields directly; copy() and mutate() delegate through builder chaining; combineWith() merges base and tool-specific state.

changes.layer: OllamaChatOptions alignment to generic builder pattern
changes.summary: OllamaChatOptions adds public no-arg and protected constructors, refactors Builder to extend DefaultToolCallingChatOptions.Builder and implement StructuredOutputChatOptions.Builder , bridges Ollama naming (numPredict→maxTokens), adds thinking mode methods returning B, and rewrites toMap() to manually filter nulls. copy()/mutate() delegate through builder; build() uses protected constructor.

changes.layer: ChatOptions test framework and Ollama test updates
changes.summary: AbstractChatOptionsTests provides reusable JUnit 5 base class verifying builder instance semantics and mutate() immutability. OllamaChatOptionsTests extends it, provides concrete class and builder hooks, and adjusts numeric assertions for float-backed options.
spring-ai-ollama adds test-scoped dependency on spring-ai-test.

issues.content: thinkOption is missing from toMap(), breaking thinking mode configuration. The thinkOption field (annotated with @JsonProperty("think")) is not included in the manually constructed map. This means all thinking mode configurations (enableThinking(), disableThinking(), thinkLow(), etc.) will be silently dropped when the options are converted to a map for API requests.

Add identity check this == o for performance. Standard equals() implementations typically check identity first before null/class checks. This avoids unnecessary field comparisons when comparing an object to itself.

Missing defensive copy for stopSequences in combineWith() creates shared mutable state. The stopSequences() setter correctly performs a defensive copy (line 80), but combineWith() directly assigns the reference from the other builder (line 122). This creates shared mutable state between builders, which could lead to unexpected aliasing if either builder's stopSequences is later modified.

toolNames(Set) stores the caller's reference instead of a defensive copy. Unlike toolCallbacks(List) (line 232, new ArrayList<>(...)), the non-null branch assigns this.toolNames = toolNames directly. This creates two concrete problems: 1. **Aliasing:** a caller mutating the passed set after toolNames(...) (but before build()) silently mutates builder state. 2. **Runtime exception on chaining:** if an immutable set is passed (e.g. toolNames(Set.of("tool1")), as used in DefaultToolCallingChatOptionsTests), a subsequent toolNames(String... ) call invokes this.toolNames.addAll(...) on an immutable set, throwing UnsupportedOperationException.

combineWith aliases mutable collections and overrides inconsistently. Two concerns in the merge logic: - Lines 310-311 assign options.toolCallbacks/options.toolNames by reference, so the two builders share the same mutable lists/sets — a later mutation on one leaks into the other. Prefer copying (new ArrayList<>(...), new HashSet<>(...)), consistent with the setters. - toolCallbacks/toolNames are overwritten unconditionally (even when other holds the empty default), while internalToolExecutionEnabled is merged only when non-null. This asymmetry means combining with a default-initialized builder clears existing tool callbacks/names. Since this path is intended for the upcoming merge rework, aligning the null/empty semantics now avoids a latent merge bug.

walkthrough: This PR refactors structured output converter abstraction by introducing a default getJsonSchema() method to the StructuredOutputConverter interface, enabling custom converters to provide schemas. DefaultChatClient simplifies its native structured-output logic by removing the BeanOutputConverter type check and using the interface method directly. New tests validate the simplified behavior with custom converter implementations.

changes.summary: NO_JSON_SCHEMA constant and default getJsonSchema() method establish the contract for any structured output converter to provide JSON schemas.
BeanOutputConverter marks getJsonSchema() with @Override annotation, explicitly implementing the interface contract.
doResponseEntity() and doSingleWithBeanOutputConverter() now call outputConverter.getJsonSchema() directly without type checking, enabling any converter implementation to provide schemas.

changes.layer: Native structured output tests with custom converters
changes.summary: Four new test methods validate ChatClient with custom StructuredOutputConverter implementations using JsonNode response type; CustomJsonSchemaOutputConverter demonstrates converter interface implementation for instruction formatting, schema provision, and response parsing.

issues.content: Consider annotating the return type with @NonNull for clarity. The Javadoc states the method should return the schema or NO_JSON_SCHEMA, and the default implementation returns a non-null value. Annotating the return type with @NonNull would make the contract explicit and align with the codebase's use of jspecify annotations (already imported in BeanOutputConverter and used in test code).

walkthrough: Adds reasoning/thinking model support to the Mistral AI Spring module. Introduces a polymorphic ContentChunk sealed interface hierarchy with custom Jackson serialization for message content, a ReasoningEffort enum and FinishReason enum in the API, threads reasoningEffort through MistralAiChatOptions, and refactors MistralAiChatModel to extract reference and thinking metadata. Includes comprehensive unit and integration tests for thinking models, citation workflows, and the new content type system.

changes.layer: FinishReason enum, ReasoningEffort, and ChatCompletionRequest wiring
changes.summary: Introduces FinishReason enum replacing ChatCompletionFinishReason, adds ReasoningEffort enum and reasoning_effort record field to ChatCompletionRequest, updates all shortcut constructors, switches Choice/ChunkChoice finish reason types, makes FunctionTool.Function.description nullable, and refactors ResponseFormat schema handling.
Adds the optional reasoningEffort field with getter, threads it through the protected constructor, equals/hashCode, the AbstractBuilder setter, combineWith, mutate, and build.

changes.layer: MistralAiChatModel metadata helpers, request creation, and media handling
changes.summary: Adds REFERENCE_CONTENT_METADATA, REFERENCE_THINKING_CONTENT_METADATA, THINKING_CONTENT_METADATA constants, refactors buildMetadata/buildGeneration, introduces calculateToolsRequestParameter, replaces Base64/MediaContent image handling with ImageUrlChunk helpers, and aggregates streaming via MessageAggregator.
Replaces ChatCompletionFinishReason with MistralAiApi.FinishReason in chunk-merge logic and the tool-call finish check.

Adds @ThinkingModelSource JUnit annotation for parameterized tests over three thinking-capable models, and ThinkingModelUtils interface with THINKING_MODELS, provideChatModelValue, provideReasoningEffort helpers.

Adds entity/stream thinking model tests, citations/references test, referenceCall/thinkingCall/thinkingStream tests, and helper methods for prompt construction, metadata assertion, and reference JSON loading.

Comprehensive unit tests for ChatCompletionMessage serialization, deserialization error cases, and content extraction helpers, backed by content_chunks.json, content_chunks_message.json, and text_message.json.

changes.layer: Test cleanup, options tests, retry tests, and runtime hints
changes.summary: Adds reasoningEffort assertions to options tests; refactors retry tests to programmatic mock setup; updates request tests for chunk-based content assertions; tightens test class/member visibility across API tool ITs; adds FinishReason runtime hints assertion; replaces pom test dependency with jsonassert.

issues.content: Handle nullable content in ContentDeserializer. ChatCompletionMessage.content is nullable (Line 1182), but deserialization currently throws on VALUE_NULL. This will fail on valid payloads containing "content": null.

Fix duplicated tools entry in hashCode (Line 362). hashCode currently hashes this.tools twice and skips this.toolNames, while equals compares toolNames. This increases collision risk for option objects that only differ by tool names.

Use stricter type-name matching for critical class verification. Line [133] uses substring matching, which can pass on unrelated type names and hide missing hints. Prefer endsWith(...) (or exact expected names) for both $ and . nested-class forms.

Relax over-constrained LLM assertions to reduce flaky integration failures. Line 102 and Lines 198-210 assert exact lexical/chunk shapes ("bananas", "apples", exact size/order of 3 chunks). These are brittle for generative responses and can fail even when citation/content contracts are valid. Prefer contract-level assertions: non-empty text, presence of at least one ReferenceChunk with non-empty IDs, and tolerant token variants. Apply the same pattern to models/spring-ai-mistral-ai/src/test/java/org/springframework/ai/mistralai/MistralAiChatModelIT.java Line 210 (avoid exact List.of(0) equality).

Guard function lookup before invocation. Line [125] can throw NullPointerException when the model returns an unexpected function name. Add an explicit lookup assertion (or fail-fast message) before calling .apply(...) to make failures deterministic and diagnosable.

Create a per-test retry template instance instead of mutating the shared SHORT_RETRY_TEMPLATE. RetryUtils.SHORT_RETRY_TEMPLATE is a shared static instance initialized once at class load time. In beforeEach() (lines 74–76), the test obtains this shared instance and mutates it via setRetryListener(), replacing the default listener. Since all tests reuse the same static instance and each test modifies its listener, this creates test interference and order-dependent behavior. If tests run in parallel, this causes a race condition. Create a fresh RetryTemplate for each test instead: java @BeforeEach void beforeEach() { // Create a new template per test instead of mutating the shared instance RetryTemplate retryTemplate = RetryUtils.createShortRetryTemplate(); // or similar this.retryListener = new TestRetryListener(); retryTemplate.setRetryListener(this.retryListener); // ... rest of setup } Also applies to lines 86–91 where the mutated template is passed to both model builders.

Use value equality for response text assertions. Lines 110 and 148 use isSameAs("Response"), which asserts object identity. For text content, use value equality (isEqualTo) to avoid brittle assertions that depend on string interning behavior.
